cfg.geo.jq_busy: jq is being installed. Wait for it to finish.

cfg.geo.no_xkeen_body: Geodata lists are updated through XKeen. Install XKeen on the “Services” page to use this tab.

cfg.geo.run_confirm_body: xkeen -ug will update all databases and restart the running kernel.
cfg.geo.run_failed: Could not start the database update: {reason}.
cfg.geo.reason_html: got HTML instead of a database
cfg.geo.reason_run_network: network unavailable, XKeen did not start downloading
cfg.geo.reason_timeout: the run did not finish in time
cfg.geo.reason_failed_new: the new file was not downloaded
cfg.geo.reason_exit: the process exited with an error
cfg.geo.reason_foreign_ref: configs outside the panel use the file
cfg.geo.reason_remove_failed: the file could not be removed
cfg.geo.reason_xkeen_json_invalid: xkeen.json could not be read or failed validation
cfg.geo.reason_comments_lost: the edit would remove comments from xkeen.json
cfg.geo.res_unverified: SHA-256 not verified: GitHub API unavailable.
cfg.geo.res_unverified_limit: SHA-256 not verified: GitHub limit, retry in an hour.
cfg.geo.parse_unknown: Per-file result could not be determined, see the output.
cfg.geo.gips_status: GeoIPSET: {status}. It cannot be managed from the panel.
cfg.geo.waiting_apply: The run is waiting for Apply to finish.
cfg.geo.cron_found: XKeen cron has a database update job: {schedule}. Adopt this schedule in the panel? Until you confirm, XKeen cron keeps working as before.
cfg.geo.cron_adopted: Schedule adopted. The XKeen cron job was removed.
cfg.geo.cron_two: The XKeen cron job is back ({schedule}): databases update on two schedules.
cfg.geo.cron_failed: Could not change the cron job: {reason}.
cfg.geo.cron_suspended: The panel schedule is suspended: while the flag was off, XKeen cron updated the databases ({schedule}). Adopt the schedule again?
cfg.geo.cron_nonstandard: XKeen cron has a database update job with a non-standard schedule ({schedule}). The panel does not adopt it; remove it by hand so the databases are not updated twice.

cfg.geo.ghproxy_hint: Proxy address XKeen uses to download from GitHub. Empty means direct.
cfg.geo.ghproxy_suggest: GitHub is not reachable directly. Set a proxy in the field above.
cfg.geo.nojq: jq is not found: XKeen cannot read geodata entries without it.
cfg.geo.jq_failed: Could not install jq: {reason}. Output below.
cfg.geo.update_off: Database updates are turned off in XKeen settings (geofile_update: false). While off, XKeen downloads nothing.
cfg.geo.group_standard_desc: XKeen downloads and updates these files. Turning one off removes the file from the router.
cfg.geo.group_panel_desc: An enabled set is a permanent geodata entry in xkeen.json.
cfg.geo.group_own_desc: Sources of the form "file name + URL", including those added to xkeen.json by hand.
cfg.geo.chip_dup_url: URL differs from the standard one
cfg.geo.chip_draft_off: will be turned off after Apply
cfg.geo.chip_invalid: invalid entry: XKeen will not process the following ones
cfg.geo.dup_hint: The file is already on disk and XKeen's standard branch updates it. The geodata entry downloads it a second time.
cfg.geo.dup_url_hint: After each update the file keeps whatever was downloaded last.
cfg.geo.own_empty_body: Add a file by URL: XKeen downloads it and updates it with the standard databases.
cfg.geo.enable_body_standard: A temporary geodata entry will appear in xkeen.json: {file}. XKeen downloads the file on update; the panel then removes the entry and XKeen keeps updating the file itself. The previous xkeen.json is backed up, comments are kept.
cfg.geo.enable_body_panel: A permanent geodata entry will appear in xkeen.json: {file}. XKeen downloads the file and updates it with the other databases. The previous xkeen.json is backed up, comments are kept.
cfg.geo.enable_done: Set enabled. XKeen will download the file.
cfg.geo.cleanup_done: {file} downloaded. The temporary geodata entry was removed from xkeen.json; XKeen updates the file from now on.
cfg.geo.cleanup_stuck: {file} downloaded, but the temporary geodata entry could not be removed: xkeen.json was edited by hand. Open Lists and press "Finish enabling".
cfg.geo.add_check_hint: "Add" becomes available after the check. Any edit resets the result.
cfg.geo.add_fill_hint: Fill in the file name and URL.
cfg.geo.check_route: The check uses the same route as XKeen's download: {route}.
cfg.geo.chk_name_bad: The name must end with .dat and must not contain /, \ or "..".
cfg.geo.chk_name_taken: The name is taken: {file} (a standard set or another entry).
cfg.geo.chk_scheme_http: Unencrypted: the file can be tampered with in transit.
cfg.geo.chk_scheme_bad: Only http and https addresses are accepted.
cfg.geo.chk_reach_fail: The address did not respond: {reason}. It may be a network problem; you can still add the source.
cfg.geo.chk_size_none: The server does not report a file size: XKeen will skip this download.
cfg.geo.chk_size_small: The file is smaller than 24 KB: XKeen will not download it.
cfg.geo.chk_html: The link returns an HTML page, not a dat database: XKeen will not download it.
cfg.geo.chk_not_dat: The content does not look like a dat database.
cfg.geo.chk_heavy: The file is large ({size}): Xray starts slower and uses more memory.
cfg.geo.chk_space: Not enough space in the dat directory: need {need}, {free} free.
cfg.geo.chk_gh_hint: If GitHub is not reachable directly, set a proxy in the Download block.
cfg.geo.chk_proxy_all: gh_proxy applies to all links: XKeen will fetch a non-GitHub address through the proxy too.
cfg.geo.chk_gh_unreachable: GitHub is not reachable this way: XKeen will not start updating the databases. Set a proxy in the Download block.
cfg.geo.url_name_fixed: The file name cannot be changed. A different name is a new source, and the old one is deleted.
cfg.geo.dup_body: The entry will be removed from xkeen.json, the file stays. XKeen's standard branch will update it from now on.
cfg.geo.finish_include_body: {file} is already on the router. The panel will remove the temporary geodata entry so the file is not downloaded twice.
cfg.geo.finish_delete_body: The configs no longer reference {file}. The panel will remove the geodata entry and the file.
cfg.geo.del_loading: Looking for references to the file…
cfg.geo.del_summary_one: Rules reference lists of this file: {count} rule.
cfg.geo.del_summary_few: Rules reference lists of this file: {count} rules.
cfg.geo.del_summary_many: Rules reference lists of this file: {count} rules.
cfg.geo.act_label: What to do with the list {file} · {tag}
cfg.geo.replace_hint: The same tag in another file: {file} · {tag}.
cfg.geo.del_rule_dies: Rule {n} will be deleted: there are no other conditions.
cfg.geo.del_effects: After Apply the panel first writes configs for both kernels without references to the file, then removes the geodata entry and the file{symlink}. The panel never changes dat contents.
cfg.geo.del_nolinks: Nothing references the file. The file and its geodata entry will be deleted after Apply.
cfg.geo.del_foreign: Configs not managed by the panel use this file: {places}. Deletion is blocked. Take routing into the panel or edit the file in the Editor.
cfg.geo.del_toast: The source was moved to the draft. The file is deleted after Apply.
cfg.geo.del_incomplete: Deletion of {file} is not finished: {reason}. Configs are clean; the file is still present and updated. Open Lists and press "Finish".
cfg.geo.step_remove: Removing the geodata entry and file {file}
cfg.geo.insp_tags_capped: Showing the first {shown} of {total} tags. Narrow the search.
cfg.geo.lookup_make_rule: Create a rule with this list
cfg.geo.mihomo_desc: Mihomo takes lists from XKeen databases. The panel neither reads nor changes these files.
cfg.geo.notice_file_kept: Database update: {file} — kept the old one: {reason}.
cfg.geo.notice_run_failed: The database update failed: {reason}. Retry in an hour.
cfg.geo.notice_retry_failed: The database update retry failed: {reason}. The next run is on schedule.
cfg.geo.err.actions_invalid: Choose a valid action for every affected list.
cfg.geo.err.already_present: A geodata entry with this name or URL is already in xkeen.json.
cfg.geo.err.apply_busy: Apply is running. Wait for it to finish.
cfg.geo.err.comments_lost: xkeen.json contains comments and writing would remove them. Confirm the loss of comments.
cfg.geo.err.cron_failed: Could not change the XKeen cron job.
cfg.geo.err.remove_failed: Could not remove the list file. The source stays in Lists; press "Finish" again.
cfg.geo.err.write_failed: Could not write xkeen.json. The source stays in Lists; press "Finish" again.
cfg.geo.err.cron_missing: The XKeen cron job was not found; it may have been removed already.
cfg.geo.err.cron_nonstandard: The XKeen cron schedule is non-standard: the panel does not adopt it. Remove the job by hand.
cfg.geo.err.draft_conflict: The draft was changed in another tab. The fresh version is shown — repeat the action.
cfg.geo.err.entry_not_found: There is no geodata entry with this URL in xkeen.json; it may have been removed already. The list was refreshed.
cfg.geo.err.foreign_ref: Configs not managed by the panel use this file, deletion is blocked. Take routing into the panel or edit the file in the Editor.
cfg.geo.err.geodata_busy: The manager is busy: databases are updating, jq is installing or an entry is being cleaned up. Wait for it to finish.
cfg.geo.err.geodata_changed: xkeen.json changed while the dialog was open. The dialog was refreshed; review the changes and retry.
cfg.geo.err.geofile_update_off: Database updates are off in the XKeen settings (geofile_update). Turn them on and try again.
cfg.geo.err.invalid_json: xkeen.json cannot be parsed as JSON. Fix the file in the Editor and try again.
cfg.geo.err.invalid_structure: The structure of xkeen.json is unexpected. Fix the file in the Editor and try again.
cfg.geo.err.kernel_op_in_progress: A kernel operation is in progress: install, switch or update. Try again when it finishes.
cfg.geo.err.list_not_found: There is no such list in the file.
cfg.geo.err.lookup_query: Enter a domain or an IP address.
cfg.geo.err.mode_invalid: Unknown mode: only deleting and turning off are accepted.
cfg.geo.err.name_invalid: The name must end with .dat and must not contain /, \ or "..".
cfg.geo.err.name_taken: The name is taken: {file} (a standard set or another entry).
cfg.geo.err.no_jq: XKeen needs jq to write geodata. Install it in the Download block and try again.
cfg.geo.err.not_pending: The source is already fine: there is nothing to finish.
cfg.geo.err.probe_blocked: The source check failed: fix the problems found and check again.
cfg.geo.err.raw_ref: The file is referenced in raw rules that the panel does not parse. Remove the references from them and try again.
cfg.geo.err.schedule_invalid: The schedule is invalid: a weekday or "daily", an hour from 0 to 23 and a minute from 0 to 59 are required.
cfg.geo.err.set_unknown: There is no such set in the catalog.
cfg.geo.err.update_failed: The entry was written but the databases could not be updated: run xkeen -ug manually or press "Update now".
cfg.geo.err.update_unavailable: Database update is unavailable right now. The entry was written; update the databases later.
cfg.geo.err.url_invalid: The URL is invalid: only http and https addresses are accepted.
cfg.geo.err.xkeen_json_invalid: Could not read xkeen.json: the file is damaged. Fix it in the Editor.
cfg.geo.err.xkeen_missing: XKeen is not installed. Install it and try again.
cfg.geo.err.xkeen_too_old: This XKeen version cannot update custom databases (2.0.1 or newer is required). Update XKeen with xkeen -uk.
cfg.geo.err.unknown: The action failed. Try again; if the error persists, reload the page.
cfg.sec.comments_ack: I agree to lose the comments
cfg.sec.comments_warn: The files {files} contain comments. The panel does not store them: they will be lost on takeover. The original file with the comments stays in the backups.
cfg.sec.take_files: The panel will keep these in the backups: {files}. The section values move to the panel and the core keeps working as before.
cfg.sec.foreign_note: The section is managed by {owner} ({file}). The effective values are shown here, as the core merges them. You can edit them after taking the section over to the panel.
cfg.sec.empty_body: Install the core on the “Services” page to configure its sections.
cfg.sec.no_file: There is no section file in configs/. On takeover it is filled with preset values.
cfg.sec.list_empty: The list is empty. Add the first row with the button below the list.
cfg.sec.kernel_stopped: The core is stopped. Changes take effect when it starts.
cfg.sec.err_port: The port is an integer from 1 to 65535.
cfg.sec.err_tag_required: Set a tag: rules find the inbound by it.
cfg.sec.err_duplicate: {what} “{value}” already exists in this section. Set another value.
cfg.sec.raw_syntax: Syntax error on line {line}: {detail}. Fix the text — the draft is not updated until then.
cfg.sec.raw_reserved: The key “{key}” is managed by the panel and cannot be set here. {hint}
cfg.sec.controller_secret: A TCP external-controller address exposes the core API to the network. Set a non-empty secret or remove the key: the panel uses the unix socket.
cfg.sec.take_changed: The file {file} changed after the check. Open the dialog again and repeat the takeover.
cfg.sec.restart_xkeen: Changing the port restarts XKeen with xkeen -restart: connections drop and the iptables rules are rebuilt.
cfg.sec.restart_tun: Changing tun requires a full Mihomo restart instead of a hot reload.
cfg.sec.restart_profile: Changing the profile fully restarts Mihomo: connections will drop.
cfg.sec.pinned_note: The panel adds these values itself: “Traffic”, XKeen and the core API rely on them. They cannot be changed.
cfg.sec.sb_note: The speed balancer mode (xkeen -sb) is replaced by the “auto” group.
cfg.sec.release_body: The original file is restored from the backup, the panel file is deleted and the changes made in the panel are dropped. The core picks this up on “Apply”.
cfg.sec.preset_title: Replace the values of the section “{name}” with the preset values?
cfg.sec.preset_body: The current values of the section in the draft will be overwritten.
cfg.sec.all_panel: The panel manages all sections of the core.
cfg.sec.owner_pending_note: The section moves under panel control on “Apply”.
cfg.sec.owner_releasing_note: Release is waiting for “Apply”: the panel still manages the section. Values are read-only; “Manage in panel” cancels the release.
cfg.sec.no_file_note: There is no section file. On takeover it is filled from the preset.
cfg.sec.drift_note: The file {file} was changed outside the panel. “Apply” is blocked until the discrepancy is resolved.
cfg.sec.mihomo_section_note: The section belongs to the profile: it is taken and released together with it.
cfg.sec.drift_foreign: A foreign file {file} with the section key appeared in configs/. “Apply” is blocked: restore the panel file or release control.
cfg.sec.blocked.inbounds_mixed: The inbounds are in the file {file} together with other keys. Move inbounds to a separate file or edit in the Editor.
cfg.sec.blocked.section_shadowed: The file {file} comes after the panel file and would override it. Remove the key from that file or rename the file.
cfg.sec.blocked.xkeen_too_old: Inbounds can be taken over with XKeen 2.0 or newer.
cfg.sec.take_title_one: Take the section “{name}” over to the panel
cfg.sec.take_title_all: Take all {kernel} sections over to the panel
cfg.sec.take_no_file: There is no section file in configs/: it is filled with preset values.
cfg.sec.take_releasing: The release is cancelled: the panel's previous value comes back.
cfg.sec.take_force_proxy: The force-proxy inbounds stay with XKeen. The panel puts the rule “these inbounds → {group}” first. The speed balancer mode (xkeen -sb) is replaced by the “auto” group.
cfg.sec.take_consequence: The change goes to the draft and the files change on “Apply”. “Release control” restores the original file.
cfg.sec.profile_foreign: The Mihomo profile ({name}) is managed by {owner}. Mihomo sections are taken over to the panel together with its routing.
cfg.sec.profile_releasing: Releasing Mihomo is waiting for “Apply”: the panel still manages the profile (xcp-main.yaml).
cfg.sec.take_routing_sections: The values of the profile sections (DNS, inbounds, TUN, sniffer and other keys) are moved to the panel once. Routing (proxies, rules and so on) is rebuilt by the panel.

cfg.sec.err.draft_open: There are unapplied changes. Apply or discard them, then try again.

cfg.sec.err.group_not_found: The group “{group}” was not found. Choose another group.
cfg.sec.err.inbound_duplicate: An inbound tag or an address and port pair is repeated. Set another value.
cfg.sec.err.inbound_port_invalid: The port is an integer from 1 to 65535.
cfg.sec.err.inbounds_mixed: The inbounds are in the file {file} together with other keys. Move inbounds to a separate file or edit in the Editor.
cfg.sec.err.invalid_input: Invalid value ({key}). Fix it and try again.
cfg.sec.err.kernel_not_installed: The {kernel} core is not installed. Install it on the “Services” page.

cfg.sec.err.nothing_to_reclaim: Nothing to restore: there are no discrepancies.
cfg.sec.err.raw_dup_key: The key “{key}” is repeated in the “Advanced” text. Keep one.

cfg.sec.err.raw_too_large: The “Advanced” text is too large. Shorten it.
cfg.sec.err.section_not_managed: The panel does not manage this section. Take it over to the panel and try again.
cfg.sec.err.section_shadowed: The file {file} comes after the panel file and would override it. Remove the key from that file or rename the file.
cfg.sec.err.section_unknown: There is no such section. Reload the page.
cfg.sec.err.xkeen_too_old: Inbounds can be taken over with XKeen 2.0 or newer. Update XKeen and try again.

cfg.hint.force_proxy_group_missing: The group for force-proxy inbounds was deleted. Choose a group in the “Inbounds” section.
cfg.sec.raw_hint.routing: Rules are edited on the “Groups” and “Rules” tabs.
cfg.sec.raw_hint.pinned: The panel adds this value itself.
cfg.sec.raw_hint.section: This key is edited in its own section.
cfg.sec.raw_hint.profile: The panel adds store-selected itself. The other profile subkeys are in “Advanced” of the “General” section.

cfg.prof.title: Profiles

cfg.prof.load_error: Could not load profiles. Check the connection to the router and try again.

cfg.prof.sum_nodes_many: Nodes: {sources} enabled sources, {count} nodes. They are supplied by the panel source files and update on their own; there is no need to put the subscription into the profile.

cfg.prof.sum_copy_user: The copy is byte for byte: the panel changes nothing in it.
cfg.prof.sum_unix_old: Mihomo on the router is older than v1.18.4 and does not know external-controller-unix: the API will not work with this profile.

cfg.prof.err_preview: Could not get the profile contents. Try again: creation is unavailable without them.
cfg.prof.err_prev_target: Mihomo returns to this profile when released. Renaming is unavailable while the panel manages Mihomo.
cfg.prof.rolled_back: Mihomo did not start with profile “{name}”: {reason}. The panel restored the previous state.
cfg.prof.filled_toast: Values moved into the draft. Check the sections and press “Apply”.
cfg.prof.to_user_body: Mihomo stops taking its settings from the panel and starts with this profile. The xcp-main.yaml file is deleted and rebuilt on return; the panel keeps the Mihomo section values and restores them. Mihomo restarts and connections drop. If it does not start, the panel restores everything as it was.
cfg.prof.to_user_adopt: The regular config.yaml file is moved to profiles/config-xkeen.yaml unchanged. You can return to it with “Make active” on config-xkeen. If Mihomo does not start, the file is put back.
cfg.prof.xray_stays: Xray routing stays with the panel.
cfg.prof.to_panel_title: Give Mihomo back to the panel?
cfg.prof.to_panel_body: The panel rebuilds xcp-main.yaml from groups, rules and sources, and Mihomo restarts with it. Section values return to what they were before the switch. Keys of your profile are not carried over — you can pick them up later with “Fill from profile”. Profile “{name}” stays in the list.
cfg.prof.delete_body: A copy is kept in the panel backups. Mihomo keeps running with the active profile.
cfg.prof.dep_source: Profiles that reference this source file: {profiles}. After deletion proxy_providers/xcp-{id}.yaml disappears and Mihomo will not find nodes in these profiles. The panel does not edit them.
cfg.prof.dep_check_failed: Could not check which profiles use these files.
cfg.prof.fill_no_profiles: There are no other profiles: choose a template.
cfg.prof.fill_body: Mihomo section values (general, DNS, inbounds and TUN, sniffer, other keys) are copied from the chosen source. Routing (proxies, proxy-groups, rules, providers) is built by the panel itself and is not copied.
cfg.prof.fill_warn: The current values of these sections in the draft will be replaced. The changes reach the file on “Apply”.
cfg.prof.fill_error: Values not copied: {reason}. The draft is unchanged.
xlog.take_title_on: Take the “Log” section and turn on the access log
xlog.take_title_off: Take the “Log” section and turn off the access log
xlog.take_restart_note: Xray will restart and active connections will drop.
xlog.foreign_note: The “Log” section is managed by {owner}. Turning it on hands the section over to the panel.
xlog.draft_block: There are unapplied changes. Apply or discard them in the “Configuration” section, then try again. The “Log” section changes owner only as a separate step.
xlog.disable_confirm_title: Turn off the Xray access log?
xlog.disable_confirm_msg: Xray will restart and active connections will drop. New entries will stop being added.
xlog.enable_confirm_stopped_msg: Every connection is written to flash storage and the file grows quickly — turn the log off when you do not need it. It will be written to {path}. Takes effect when Xray starts.
xlog.enabled_stopped_toast: Xray access log is on. Takes effect when Xray starts.
xlog.disabled_stopped_toast: Xray access log is off. Takes effect when Xray starts.
xlog.test_failed: Xray did not accept the configuration: {reason}. Files are unchanged.
xlog.path_denied: The access log is written to {path}, but “Logs” read files only inside /opt/var/log. Set a path inside /opt/var/log in the “Log” section on the “Xray │ Mihomo” tab.
cfg.sec.log_access_hint: Empty — the access log is off (the panel writes none).
cfg.sec.log_access_denied: The path is outside /opt/var/log: “Logs” cannot read this file.
rules.tabs_need_api: “{diag}” and “{all}” work through the Mihomo API — they become available once it starts.
rules.tabs_need_api_down: “{diag}” and “{all}” work through the Mihomo API — it is not configured or not responding.
rules.offline_note: The core performs updates: the buttons work once Mihomo is running. Showing provider files of the active profile “{profile}”.
rules.provider_no_file_http: No file yet: the core downloads it on start.
rules.provider_no_file_local: File {path} not found: the core cannot load this list. Put the file at this path or fix path in the profile.
rules.probe_proxy_not_found: the proxy is not in the running core
rules.probe_core_503: core: 503, the probe through the proxy failed
rules.probe_core_504: core: 504, the proxy did not answer in time
rules.probe_core_timeout: the core did not answer in time
rules.url_via_proxy_nocode: The core does not report the HTTP code.
rules.url_verdict_node: The problem is the node or proxy “{proxy}”: the link opens directly.
rules.url_verdict_both: The link opens neither through the proxy nor directly: check the address or a possible block.
rules.url_verdict_ok: The link is reachable through the proxy.
rules.url_direct_only: Checked directly: the core downloads via “{proxy}”, the result may differ.
svc.mihomo_no_api: The Mihomo API is not configured — charts, groups and quotas are unavailable.
svc.mihomo_no_api_hint: Add external-controller-unix to the profile or switch back to the panel profile.
svc.mihomo_started_no_api: Mihomo started without an API: charts, groups and quotas are unavailable.
cfg.sec.mihomo_release_body: Mihomo goes back to profile “{name}” and restarts, connections drop. The xcp-main.yaml file is deleted; the panel keeps the Mihomo section values and restores them when you take it again.
cfg.sec.mihomo_release_failed: Could not release Mihomo: {reason}. Nothing changed.
cfg.routing.mihomo_own_profile: Does not apply to Mihomo: profile {name} is active.
cfg.routing.release_body_own_profile: XKeen routing files return from the backup. Groups and rules stay in the draft but stop taking effect. The Mihomo profile does not change.
errors.path_not_allowed: the file is outside the config folders the panel may read. Pick a file in /opt/etc/xray or /opt/etc/mihomo.
errors.login_locked: Too many failed sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.session_expired: Your session ended. Sign in again.
errors.router_unreachable: The router isn't responding. Check that it's on and the panel is running.
errors.timeout: The router didn't respond in time. Try again.
errors.permission_denied: No permission for this file. Check its owner and mode in Entware.
errors.file_not_found: File not found. It may have been deleted or renamed.
errors.no_space: The router's storage is full. Free up space and try again.
errors.server_error: router error (code {code}), see the panel logs for details
svc.restart_hint: The service stops for a few seconds; connections reconnect
svc.stop_hint: Proxying through this service stops until it is started again
settings.tab_general_desc: Language, theme, accent color, status widget, behavior
dash.pulse.no_xkeen_sub: Proxying on the router doesn't work without it
dash.pulse.no_kernel_sub: Install Xray or Mihomo in Services
dash.pulse.running_warn_sub: Traffic goes through the proxy, with warnings
cfg.dns.title: Router DNS interception
cfg.dns.subtitle: All DNS queries from the router and devices go through the core and the selected node group instead of the ISP.
cfg.dns.firmware_note: Before interception was enabled, DNS was served by the firmware, and after it is disabled the firmware serves it again.
cfg.dns.scope_note: Interception applies to the whole router: all segments, including the guest one, and devices outside the XKeen policy get DNS through the core in the same way.
cfg.dns.upstreams_via: Via the “{group}” group. If the group does not respond, DNS stays silent: queries never go out directly.
cfg.dns.nodes_value: Public DoH directly; if it is unreachable, the firmware resolver.
cfg.dns.ipv6_off: The router has no IPv6: listening on IPv4 only.
cfg.dns.check_none: No check has been run yet.
cfg.dns.unavailable_body: Interception is unavailable on this router: the firmware does not support the opkg dns-override command. DNS stays with the firmware. The other DNS section fields work as before.
cfg.dns.zones_empty: No custom zones. Add a zone with the button below the list.
cfg.dns.check_off_hint: The check goes through 127.0.0.1:53, so interception must be enabled.
cfg.dns.banner_enable: Router DNS is now served by {kernel}. If the network works, press “Keep”. Otherwise in {seconds} s the panel will return DNS to the firmware on its own.
cfg.dns.banner_apply: DNS changes have been applied. If the network works, press “Keep”. Otherwise in {seconds} s the panel will roll back this apply, and interception will stay enabled.
cfg.dns.banner_switch: DNS interception has moved to {kernel}. If the network works, press “Keep”. Otherwise in {seconds} s the panel will return DNS to the firmware, and the core will remain {kernel}.
cfg.dns.keep_error: Could not confirm: {reason}. The window continues.
cfg.dns.toast_rolled_apply: The apply was rolled back. The edits are back in the draft.
cfg.dns.toast_timeout: DNS returned to the firmware: interception was not confirmed within {seconds} s.
cfg.dns.toast_legacy_off: The old DNS redirection is turned off.
cfg.dns.outcome_panel_restart: Rolled back: the panel restarted before interception was confirmed, {time}.
cfg.dns.outcome_watchdog: DNS returned to the firmware: the {kernel} core did not respond on 127.0.0.1:53, {time}.
cfg.dns.outcome_kernel_changed: DNS returned to the firmware: the core was changed outside the panel ({from} → {to}), {time}. Enable interception again.
cfg.dns.outcome_waiting: Interception will come back on its own once the core starts and the resolution check passes, without a confirmation window.
cfg.dns.notice_event: DNS interception changed without your involvement. Details are in the “Router DNS interception” card.
cfg.dns.status_firmware: Router DNS is served by the firmware.
cfg.dns.status_window: Interception is on, waiting for your confirmation: {n} s left.
cfg.dns.status_waiting: Interception is wanted, but DNS is currently served by the firmware: {reason}.
cfg.dns.status_disable_failed: Interception stays on: turning it off did not finish. Try “Disable interception” again.
cfg.dns.reason_kernel_stopped: the core was stopped by the panel
cfg.dns.reason_network: the panel is not reachable over the network
cfg.dns.reason_server: the panel could not complete the request
cfg.dns.block_window: Confirm interception or roll it back in the banner at the top of the page.
cfg.dns.block_stopped: Start the core. Enabling interception does not start it.
cfg.dns.block_section: The DNS section is managed by {owner}. Take it into the panel: interception writes its own values into it.
cfg.dns.block_routing: The core routing is not managed by the panel. Take it into the panel on the “Groups” and “Rules” tabs: the interception :53 listener is produced by the routing generator.
cfg.dns.block_group: There is no group for DNS queries. Take routing into the panel on the “Groups” and “Rules” tabs.
cfg.dns.fail_rolled_back: Router DNS and the core config were returned to their state before enabling.
cfg.dns.fail_rollback_failed: Rollback did not complete: {reason}. Router DNS may not respond as expected. Check resolution and disable interception if needed.
cfg.dns.load_error: Could not load the interception state. Check the connection to the router and try again.
cfg.dns.stale_error: Could not refresh the interception state: showing the last one received.
cfg.dns.group_hint: All DNS servers go through this group, including the ones you added. If the group does not respond, DNS stays silent: queries never go out directly.
cfg.dns.group_missing: The “{name}” group was deleted: choose another one.
cfg.dns.zones_hint: Queries to these zones go directly to the firmware resolver.
cfg.dns.err_zone_format: A zone is a domain name without a scheme or path, for example office.lan.
cfg.dns.err_zone_dup: Zone “{zone}” is already among the built-in or custom zones.
cfg.dns.edit_window_hint: The change takes effect on “Apply” and will require confirmation: you will have {seconds} s.
cfg.dns.legacy_will_off: The old DNS redirection will be turned off.
cfg.dns.legacy_drift: The old DNS redirection was turned on outside the panel (xkeen -dns on). The two mechanisms do not work together on port 53.
cfg.dns.other_kernel: Interception is run by {kernel}: the {current} forms do not affect it right now.
cfg.dns.pinned_policy: local zones ({zones}) and direct-rule domains ({direct} sets)
cfg.dns.disable_body: Router DNS will return to the firmware, and the core keeps running. No confirmation window is needed.
cfg.dns.cancel_wait_body: Interception will not come back on its own when the core starts. DNS stays with the firmware.
cfg.sec.f.proxy_server_ns_hint: The core uses these servers to find the addresses of the nodes themselves, before the tunnel. Without them DNS would loop.
cfg.sec.f.fake_ip_filter_hint: Domains from the list get real addresses. While interception is on, local zones are added here automatically.
cfg.sec.f.servers_via_group: While interception is on, all servers go through the “{group}” group.
cfg.sec.fake_ip_warn: In fake-ip mode clients get service addresses from the {range} range. Devices outside the XKeen policy and services that reach such addresses directly may lose connectivity.
cfg.sec.err_listen: The address is a host and a port, for example 0.0.0.0:53.
cfg.sec.err_cidr: The range is a network address with a mask, for example 198.18.0.1/16.
cfg.dns.err.busy: Another operation is in progress. Wait for it to finish and try again.
cfg.dns.err.generic: Could not perform the action: {reason}. Nothing has changed.
cfg.dns.err.group_missing: There is no group for DNS queries. Take routing into the panel on the “Groups” and “Rules” tabs.
cfg.dns.err.group_name_invalid: The group name “{name}” cannot be passed to the core as a DNS target: it contains invalid characters. Rename the group.
cfg.dns.err.kernel_conflict: Both cores are running. Stop one of them and try again.
cfg.dns.err.kernel_stopped: Start the core. Enabling interception does not start it.
cfg.dns.err.legacy_off_failed: Could not turn off the old redirection: {reason}.
cfg.dns.err.name_invalid: The name to check is a domain name, for example example.com.
cfg.dns.err.no_window: There is no confirmation window: interception has already been confirmed or rolled back.
cfg.dns.err.override_failed: The firmware rejected the dns-override command: {detail}.
cfg.dns.err.port_busy: Port 53 is taken by another service. Free it or turn off the other interception.
cfg.dns.err.probe_external: The name {name} did not resolve through the “{group}” group. Check that the group has live nodes.
cfg.dns.err.probe_local: The local name {name} did not resolve through the firmware. Check the router DNS settings.
cfg.dns.err.restart_failed: The core did not start with the new configuration: {detail}. Look in “Logs”.
cfg.dns.err.routing_not_managed: The {kernel} routing is not managed by the panel. Take it into the panel on the “Groups” and “Rules” tabs: the interception :53 listener is produced by the routing generator.
cfg.dns.err.section_foreign: The {kernel} DNS section is not managed by the panel. Take it into the panel: interception writes its own values into it.
cfg.dns.err.self_server: The server “{server}” in the Mihomo DNS section is the router itself: the query would loop back to the interception listener. Remove it or replace it with an external one.
cfg.dns.err.unavailable: Interception is unavailable on this router: {reason}.
cfg.dns.err.window_active: Confirm interception or roll it back in the banner at the top of the page.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_group_missing: The group for DNS queries was deleted: choose another one in the “Router DNS interception” card.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_group_name_invalid: The group name “{name}” cannot be passed to the core as a DNS target: it contains invalid characters. Rename the group.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_routing_required: While interception is on, the panel manages the {kernel} routing: disable interception, then release the routing.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_section_required: While interception is on, the panel manages the core DNS section: disable interception, then release the section.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_self_server: The server “{server}” in the Mihomo DNS section is the router itself: with interception on, the query would loop back to the listener. Remove it or replace it with an external one.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_zone_dup: Zone “{zone}” is already among the built-in or custom zones.
cfg.dns.issue.dns_zone_invalid: Local zone “{zone}” is not a domain name.
